findings.evidence: Parameters.lean:307-309 `@[simp] theorem chiralCoupling_isospin_zero (q s2 : ℝ) : chiralCoupling 0 q s2 = -(q * s2)`; Parameters.lean:346-348 `@[simp] theorem ofQuantumNumbers_gR ... = chiralCoupling 0 q s2`. The author's own `ofQuantumNumbers_neutrino_gR` (Couplings.lean:138) avoids `simp` and unfolds with `gR_def` instead.
findings.fix: Drop `@[simp]` from one of the two: either make `chiralCoupling_isospin_zero` a plain lemma, or state `ofQuantumNumbers_gR` as `= -(q * s2)` and keep `chiralCoupling 0 q s2` out of simp-normal goals.
findings.issue: `@[simp] ofQuantumNumbers_gR` rewrites to `chiralCoupling 0 q s2`, but `@[simp] chiralCoupling_isospin_zero` (line 307-309) rewrites exactly that term to `-(q * s2)`. The stated RHS is therefore never the simp normal form, and `eq_ofQuantumNumbers_iff` (line 355) states a goal shape that any subsequent `simp` immediately destroys — downstream proofs that mix `rw [eq_ofQuantumNumbers_iff]` with `simp` will break unpredictably.

findings.evidence: Couplings.lean:79-82 `rw [isospinWeight_one, doubletElectricCharge_standardModel_YL_one, eq_ofQuantumNumbers_iff, gL_def, gR_def, chiralCoupling_def, chiralCoupling_def]`, identical modulo names at lines 89-92 and 99-102.
findings.fix: Prove the three goals from a gV/gA extensionality fact (`mk.injEq`, or an `ext_iff` lemma next to `ext_gL_gR`) plus `simp only [smTreeLevelCouplings_*, ofQuantumNumbers]` and `constructor <;> ring`; if the chiral route is kept, use `simp only [chiralCoupling_def]` instead of two `rw` copies.
findings.issue: The three tabulated-coupling proofs (lines 79-82, 89-92, 99-102) rewrite with `eq_ofQuantumNumbers_iff` and then immediately undo it via `gL_def, gR_def, chiralCoupling_def, chiralCoupling_def`, so the chiral characterisation is used only as a structure-splitting device; `chiralCoupling_def` is listed twice solely because `rw` hits one occurrence at a time. The resulting six-step named-rewrite chain is repeated verbatim three times and obscures the fact that the goal is a two-component arithmetic identity.

findings.evidence: `standardModel` is `@[simps]` (Representation.lean:260-261), so `standardModel_Yu : standardModel.Yu = 4/3` is a simp lemma — the same mechanism that makes `norm_num [doubletElectricCharge_apply]` work at lines 261-262, 266-267, 271-272, 276-277.
findings.issue: `singletElectricCharge_standardModel_Yu` (280-283), `_Yd` (286-289) and `_Ye` (292-295) evaluate `y/2` at a numeral but are proved by rewriting backwards through `doubletElectricCharge_standardModel_*_eq_singletElectricCharge_*` and then through a doublet lemma. A pure arithmetic value is thereby made to depend on the cross-multiplet identity, so it breaks if that identity is restated.

findings.fix: Replace `congr 1; norm_num` with `norm_num [singletElectricCharge_def]` in all three lemmas.
findings.issue: `congr 1` is used to peel `singletElectricCharge` off both sides before `norm_num`, at lines 236, 246 and 256. `congr` splitting is brittle (it can produce different or `HEq` goals as definitions change) and is unnecessary here.

summary: Proofs are short and arithmetic is left to ring/norm_num, but the new simp set is non-confluent (ofQuantumNumbers_gR's RHS is itself a simp LHS), the three smTreeLevelCouplings_*_eq_ofQuantumNumbers proofs take a detour through eq_ofQuantumNumbers_iff that they immediately undo, and three charge-value lemmas are derived backwards through an unrelated identity.
